Subject: SA-East1 scheduled driver/kernel refresh — planned rolling restarts (Dec 3 UTC window)

Hi Diego and BlueWave team,

We wanted to give you an advance notice about a planned infrastructure maintenance window in our sa-east1 (South America) region. This is a targeted driver and kernel refresh to address an upcoming security micropatch and to improve long-tail latency for short requests.

Planned window (rolling):
- Start: 2027-12-03 04:00 UTC
- End: 2027-12-03 10:00 UTC
- Expected per-node disruption: ~60–120 seconds while the node performs a fast restart and driver swap

What to expect:
- We will perform a rolling restart across GPU host pools. No single-customer full-region outage is expected; however you may see transient request retries or slightly elevated latency during the brief restart window for the shard handling your capacity.
- For customers on Dedicated capacity with pinned instances, we will attempt live migration where supported; if migration is not available, instances will be restarted once only.
- We will automatically route traffic to healthy pools and fall back to compatible model variants when capacity is constrained.

Action items for BlueWave:
- No action required before the window for most workloads. If you have long-running generation jobs scheduled within the window, we recommend rescheduling to avoid transient interruption.
- If you require a strict blackout (no restarts) during that window please reply with the list of instance IDs and we will evaluate options (may require exception and SLA adjustment).

Attachments: maintenance runbook and impact matrix attached for your ops team.
Status page: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/sa-east1-maintenance-2027-12-03

If you have tight SLA constraints, reply directly and I will loop in our SRE lead.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

On Wed, Dec 01, 2027 at 09:35 AM -03:00 Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Diego — quick answers inline:

> 1) Short consumer requests: the serving layer will attempt automatic retries for idempotent requests and will stream a brief reconnect for streaming sessions. For non-idempotent long-running generation we recommend client-side retry with idempotency token support.
> 
> 2) Long backfills: those will very likely be interrupted if they are routed to a node that restarts. We recommend rescheduling or pinning to a pool we are not touching.
> 
> Node pools in scope: sa-gpu-g1, sa-gpu-g1-burst, sa-gpu-legacy. We will not touch the sa-gpu-small testing pools.
> 
> I will also ask our SRE (Rishi) to follow up with suggested player knobs for resume/retry.
> 
> Marcus
